requirement: Send a list of text lines to an external command on stdin as newline-terminated UTF-8 and return its output lines, rejecting lines with embedded breaks, tolerating undecodable output, and raising on failure.
skeleton: run_filter validating that no line contains a break, joining lines with a trailing newline each, calling subprocess.run with input, utf-8 replace decoding, timeout and check=True, and splitting output lines.
caption: Piping lines through an external filter with subprocess.run. run_filter(argv, lines, *, timeout=10.0) materialises the lines and raises ValueError saying a line contains a line break if any holds a newline or carriage return. It sends every line terminated by a newline, so the child sees exactly one line per item, through input= with encoding utf-8 and errors replace. It captures output with the timeout and check=True, so a failing filter raises subprocess.CalledProcessError, and undecodable bytes become the U+FFFD replacement character instead of crashing. The result is stdout.splitlines(), which never yields a trailing empty string. The fixture asserts, with sys.executable -c filters, that accented lines come back uppercased, that three lines give a newline count of 3 and no lines give 0, that one line returns one item and no input returns an empty list, that a 0xff byte decodes as U+FFFD, that an embedded newline raises ValueError, and that exit 2 raises CalledProcessError.

plan.intent: Reuse a Unix text filter from Python
constraints: Lines containing a newline or carriage return raise ValueError
Every line sent is terminated by a newline
Input and output use UTF-8 and undecodable output is replaced

rationale.teaches: Use subprocess.run input= with an explicit encoding and error handler, terminate every line, and split output with splitlines.
rationale.why: Missing final newlines make line-oriented tools drop or merge records, strict decoding crashes on stray bytes, and split on newline adds a phantom empty line.

ops.docstring: Pipe lines through an external filter command.

candidates.why_wrong: The final line is sent without its newline terminator.
Strict decoding raises UnicodeDecodeError on invalid output bytes.
A line with an embedded newline silently becomes two records.
Splitting on newline leaves a trailing empty string in the result.
A failing filter returns its partial output instead of raising.
